children: Keurig Dr Pepper said Tuesday it will sell its entire minority stake in Chobani back to the yogurt maker for $800 million. It's cashing out at an opportune time.
Earlier this year, KDP added billions of dollars of debt to finance its acquisition of JDE Peet's. The Chobani sale would generate nearly $1 billion in pretax proceeds, helping it reduce debt faster.
Chobani will separately acquire KDP's manufacturing facility and warehouse in Allentown, Pa., for about $125 million, bringing total pretax proceeds to $925 million.

Keurig Dr Pepper said it plans to use the net proceeds to reduce debt as it prepares to split into two publicly traded companies-one focused on beverages and the other on coffee-following its roughly $18 billion acquisition of JDE Peet's earlier this year.

To be sure, the proceeds from the Chobani sales equal just over 3% of Keurig Dr Pepper's roughly $29 billion of debt net of cash, and investors still have to weigh the risks of integrating JDE Peet's and executing the planned separation in early 2027.
Still, Keurig Dr Pepper is getting $800 million for an investment that originated with just $300 million three years ago.

The company originally purchased a 33% stake in coffee brand La Colombe in 2023. When Chobani bought La Colombe later that year, it exchanged that holding for a 4.6% stake in Chobani-and subsequently increased its ownership to 5.9% under the distribution agreement.

Just as important, Keurig Dr Pepper isn't giving up the commercial relationship. It will continue distributing La Colombe ready-to-drink coffee and other Chobani-owned beverages through its network, while maintaining its licensing and distribution agreement for La Colombe K-Cup pods.

That combination-monetizing a noncore financial stake while preserving the business partnership-could be appealing for investors. Keurig Dr Pepper stock was little changed in Tuesday trading. Shares have gained roughly 14% this year.
